question: Is the frozen baseline drawdown primarily caused by same-day candidate crowding or a few exceptional losses, such that a slot-count or reactive exposure rule is justified?
method: Descriptive drawdown, entry-cohort, loss-streak, and contribution analysis only. No slot count, exposure target, or loss-streak rule is selected.
interpretation: The maximum drawdown is a multi-year regime path, not an isolated crowded entry cohort.
Same-day multi-position entries contain 54.0 percent of trades but only 44.0 percent of negative cohort PnL, so crowding is not disproportionately responsible for losses in this sample.
Losses are diffuse: the worst five trades contribute only 8.1 percent of gross loss, while the right tail remains material with the top five winners contributing 32.6 percent of gross profit.
A reactive loss-streak rule would be selected from an exposed path and could reduce participation in the recovery that follows a prolonged weak regime.
rejected_followups: same-day cohort cap based on this historical result
loss-streak exposure ladder fitted to the exposed drawdown
next_direction: Start append-only forward observation of the already registered vcp_leader_breakout version. Record daily candidates, rejections, simulated orders, fills, positions, exits, and data-quality state without changing the frozen rule.
